channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Water utilities in 12 states lost control of exposed PLCs — the same advisory says energy is in scope
item.description: The campaign that began around 27 July against internet-facing water controllers has now been reported in at least 12 states. The FBI and EPA public-service alert of 30 July confirms attackers reached exposed Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 PLCs, changed IP addresses and passwords to lock operators out of monitoring and control, and in at least one case modified controller logic; reported physical effects include pressure loss and localized flooding. Grid operators should not read this as somebody else’s problem. The governing federal advisory, AA26-097A, states the same actors have disrupted PLC function across several critical infrastructure sectors including energy, and its July update names Siemens S7-1200 and Schneider Modicon M340 — controllers common in balance-of-plant, substation auxiliary and DER installations. Many public power utilities also operate the water systems that were hit. - FBI/EPA public-service alert and CISA AA26-097A; The Record, Axios, SecurityWeek - Attacks from 27 Jul 2026; FBI/EPA alert 30 Jul; 12-state tally reported 4 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] 4,407 industrial controllers found answering the public internet on EtherNet/IP
item.description: A Shodan query run on 3 August returned 4,407 devices exposing port 44818, with roughly 65% in the United States, 12% in Canada and 3% in Spain. Of 22 controllers located in cities where utilities reported incidents, 19 were running firmware susceptible to CVE-2017-16740, a Modbus TCP buffer overflow affecting Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 Series B and C on firmware 21.002 and earlier, fixed in revision 21.003. Power utilities tend to assume this is a small-water-system problem, but the exposure pattern — a controller or gateway reachable over a cellular link at an unstaffed remote site, installed by a contractor and never entered in the asset register — describes substation auxiliaries, recloser controllers, DER skids and district-heating plant just as well. - Forescout Vedere Labs analysis; The Hacker News - Shodan scan data 3 Aug 2026 — reported week of 3–7 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Six agencies warn on Gunra ransomware: affiliates entering through VPN gateways and firewalls, utilities among victims
item.description: Joint advisory AA26-222A, published 10 August by CISA, the FBI, DC3, NSA, the Secret Service and South Korea’s National Police Agency, covers Gunra ransomware. Gunra appeared in April 2025 built on leaked Conti source code and has since become a ransomware-as-a-service operation recruiting affiliates through dark-web forums. The advisory says affiliates break in through exposed edge infrastructure — VPN gateways, firewall appliances and RDP-reachable systems — and run double extortion, exfiltrating before encrypting. Named victim sectors include utilities, manufacturing, transport and government. For a generation or transmission operator the realistic damage path is not the EMS but everything that supports it: outage management, work orders, settlements, engineering file shares and the virtualization layer they all run on. - CISA/FBI/NSA joint advisory AA26-222A - Published 10 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] AA26-097A update details how PLC project files are being rewritten to disable shutdown and alarm logic
item.description: The 22 July update to joint advisory AA26-097A is the clearest public description yet of the tradecraft. Iran-affiliated actors connect to internet-exposed controllers using the vendors’ own engineering software — Rockwell Studio 5000 Logix Designer, Schneider EcoStruxure Control Expert and Siemens TIA Portal — over ports 44818, 2222, 102, 502 and 22, from leased third-party-hosted infrastructure. In one US case the FBI found a downloaded project file that preserved ladder logic for downstream function while adding logic that overrode the instruction sets maintaining safe operating parameters, and disabled shutdown and alarm logic so equipment could enter unsafe states without notifying operators. Investigators cite attacks on Rockwell CompactLogix and Micro850, Schneider Modicon M340 (BMX P34) and Siemens S7-1200. The advisory says energy is among the affected sectors. - CISA/FBI/NSA/EPA joint advisory AA26-097A; SecurityWeek - Updated 22 Jul 2026 (originally published 7 Apr 2026) — campaign ongoing

item.title: [Medium] Dragos: industrial ransomware up 12% in Q2, with zero cases of direct ICS manipulation
item.description: Dragos’ Q2 2026 analysis, published 11 August, recorded 1,140 ransomware incidents at industrial organizations, up from 1,020 in Q1. Manufacturing absorbed 747 of them; ICS-adjacent firms including engineering companies and system integrators accounted for 117, and transportation and logistics 95. North America led with 514 incidents, Europe 316. The most useful finding for a utility is the absence: Dragos observed no case in the quarter where a ransomware operator directly manipulated an industrial control system, yet operations were still disrupted through IT, ERP and virtualization systems. The 117 integrator and engineering-firm victims are worth a second look — those are the organizations holding your relay settings, one-lines and remote-access credentials. - Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis Q2 2026; Help Net Security - Published 11 Aug 2026 (covering Q2 2026)

item.title: [Critical] CVSS 10 unauthenticated root command injection in Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway (ICSA-26-225-02)
item.description: CISA published 14 ICS advisories on 13 August, led by CVE-2026-19188 in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway at CVSS 10.0. The device’s ‘Net Check’ feature passes user-supplied input from the cmdPing Socket.io event to the operating system without sanitizing it, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary OS commands as root with no user interaction. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected, and CISA lists energy among the deployment sectors alongside critical manufacturing and water. These combined HMI/gateway/DTU units are inexpensive remote-monitoring boxes that turn up on solar and storage skids, small hydro, district energy and unstaffed pump or valve stations — precisely the assets least likely to appear in a NERC CIP asset list and most likely to have a cellular connection. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-225-02 - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Hitachi Energy APM Edge at CVSS 8.8 and hard-coded credentials in ANDRITZ HIPASE-250
item.description: Two items in the 13 August CISA batch land directly on power assets. ICSA-26-225-04 covers Hitachi Energy APM Edge at CVSS 8.8 in the energy sector — the asset performance management edge platform that collects condition data from transformers, breakers and rotating plant. ICSA-26-225-05 covers ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 at CVSS 8.1 for use of hard-coded credentials; HIPASE is a protection, control and automation platform used in hydro and industrial power stations. Neither is reported as exploited. The hard-coded credential case is the more awkward of the two operationally, because there is no password to rotate — the only durable control is making sure the device is unreachable from anywhere an attacker could stand. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-225-04 and ICSA-26-225-05 - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] August ICS Patch Tuesday: maximum-severity authentication bypass in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050
item.description: Siemens published 10 advisories on 11 August. The headline item (SSA-834709) is a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with elevated privileges. Siemens also fixed a critical code-execution flaw in Siveillance Video Management Servers — substation and plant CCTV — and high-severity issues in Solid Edge, Simcenter Nastran, the Siemens License Server, Simcenter Femap, Parasolid and Logo! Soft Comfort, plus medium-severity fixes in Ruggedcom devices and Desigo controllers. Schneider Electric issued advisories for NetBotz 5 and PowerChute Serial Shutdown; Phoenix Contact covered multiple PLCnext firmware flaws exploitable without authentication. Ruggedcom, Siveillance and PowerChute are the entries most likely to be inside a substation or control-house today. - Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact PSIRT via SecurityWeek - Advisories published 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco Secure Firewall ASA/FTD zero-day added to CISA KEV after denial-of-service exploitation
item.description: CISA added three vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August. CVE-2026-20349 is a heap-inspection flaw in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Firewall Threat Defense that Cisco patched after exploitation as a zero-day for denial-of-service attacks; the others are a use-after-free in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (CVE-2026-68820) and SQL injection in Metabase (CVE-2026-72898). CISA also added Progress LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037 on 7 August and Langflow, Apache Tomcat and N-able N-central flaws on 5 August. ASA and FTD frequently serve as the electronic access point between the corporate network and the ESP, and as the VPN concentrator for after-hours support; a DoS there is a loss-of-visibility event even though it is not a breach. - CISA KEV catalog additions, 5, 7 and 11 Aug 2026 - Cisco ASA/FTD added to KEV 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] CIP-015-1 internal network security monitoring: 1 October 2028 for high impact and medium with ERC
item.description: FERC approved CIP-015-1 on 26 June 2025, requiring internal network security monitoring inside the electronic security perimeter. High-impact BES Cyber Systems and medium-impact systems with external routable connectivity must comply by 1 October 2028; all other BES Cyber Systems with ERC have until 1 October 2030. The requirements cover monitoring network data feeds, detecting anomalous activity, evaluating what is detected, protecting the monitoring data itself and retaining investigation records. FERC also directed NERC to revise the standard to bring external EACMS and PACS into scope. Read against this week’s advisories the timing is pointed: INSM is precisely the capability that would surface an engineering workstation talking to a controller it has no business talking to. - FERC Order approving NERC CIP-015-1; Black & Veatch compliance guide - Approved 26 Jun 2025 — compliance 1 Oct 2028 (high/medium with ERC), 1 Oct 2030 (other with ERC)
